{"id": "73:20/q14", "question": "What is lending God a good loan?", "turns_on": "The sources differ in the readings, referents, chronology, legal scope, or explanation shown by the positions.", "positions": [{"id": "73:20/q14/p1", "position": "The good loan is voluntary charity beyond zakat.", "reasons": "IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says the goodly loan means acts beyond zakat, such as maintaining kinship ties and feeding guests. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The goodly loan includes voluntary acts of charity and worship with body and wealth, offered eagerly and beautifully while healthy and prosperous; God preserves and multiplies it. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): The good loan means voluntary charitable spending, distinct from obligatory duties whose repayment is assured; the command urges supererogatory giving. TABATABAI, d. 1402 (author): Lending God a good loan means financial donations in His cause beyond obligatory zakat. TABATABAI, d. 1402 (سماعة): In al-Qummi's tafsir, Zur'ah transmits Sama'ah's answer that a goodly loan is something other than zakat. {"id": "73:20/q15", "question": "What good is sent ahead and what reward is promised?", "turns_on": "The sources differ in the readings, referents, chronology, legal scope, or explanation shown by the positions.", "positions": [{"id": "73:20/q15/p1", "position": "Good sent ahead is better than wealth left or deferred to death.", "reasons": "RAZI-FULL, d. 606 (ابن عباس): Ibn Abbas says good deeds stored with God are better and more rewarding than wealth deferred for a bequest at death. QURTUBI-FULL, d. 671 (عمر بن الخطاب): Umar took the promise to mean that good sent ahead is better than what is left behind, inherited, or withheld through miserliness. BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 (author): What is advanced is better and more rewarding than what is deferred to a bequest at death, or than worldly goods. NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (author): What people find with God is the reward of their good deeds; the clause answers the conditional. NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 (author): What is sent ahead is better than what is left behind, and brings greater, more abundant reward. IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 (عبد الله): The Prophet contrasts wealth sent ahead with wealth left to heirs: a person’s real wealth is what they have given or prepared for the afterlife, while the heir receives what was deferred. BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 (author): The promised reward exceeds that of a bequest made during terminal illness, whose recompense might come in worldly life. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (author): Whatever good a person sends ahead, whether already mentioned or not, will be found with God as a better and greater reward than what is deferred until a deathbed bequest. BURSEVI, d. 1127 (النبي عليه السلام): A Prophetic report says every person arrives according to what he sent ahead and regrets what he left behind.
